unit.title: Cleft Sentences & Emphasis
unit.subtitle: Focusing one element with ser + relative

grammar.title: Spotlight one word with a cleft
grammar.intro: A cleft sentence (oración enfática / perífrasis de relativo) splits a neutral sentence to spotlight a single element. You frame the focus between a form of ser and a relative word: Fue Ana quien lo hizo (It was Ana who did it), Es aquí donde vivo (This is where I live). It is the everyday way advanced speakers add emphasis without raising their voice.

sections.heading: ser + focus + relative
sections.body: Take the neutral sentence, lift out the element you want to stress, and rebuild it as ser + that element + a relative: Ana lo hizo → Fue Ana quien lo hizo. ser introduces the focus and the relative word reconnects the rest of the clause.

ex.en: It was Ana who did it.

sections.heading: Pick the right relative
sections.body: Match the relative to the kind of element in focus: quien (or el que) for people, donde for places, cuando for time, como for manner. With a preposition the whole phrase moves: Es por eso por lo que… (That's why…).

ex.en: It was then that I understood everything.

sections.heading: Lo que … es …
sections.body: A second cleft frames a whole idea with lo que + clause and then es + the focus: Lo que necesito es descansar (What I need is to rest). The colloquial opener lo que pasa es que… softly introduces an explanation.

ex.en: What I need is to rest.

ex.es: Lo que pasa es que no me avisaron.
ex.en: The thing is, they didn't tell me.

sections.heading: Ser agrees with the tense
sections.body: The verb ser normally copies the tense of the main clause: past focus → fue, present → es, future → será. When the focus is plural, ser and the relative may agree in the plural: Fueron ellos quienes vinieron.

ex.en: It was they who decided it.
It will be in June that we sign.

takeaways: Match the relative: people → quien, place → donde, time → cuando, manner → como.
Lo que + clause + es + focus highlights a whole idea: Lo que necesito es descansar.
Ser copies the tense/number: fue… quien, fueron… quienes, es… donde.

mistakes.why: For a highlighted person, careful register prefers quien (or la que) over bare que.
A focused place takes donde, not que ('que galicado').
A focused time takes cuando, not que.

exercises.prompt_en: It was then that I understood it all.
exercises.no: A focused time takes cuando, not que: “Fue entonces cuando…”.
A focused place takes donde: “Es aquí donde nos conocimos”.

exercises.prompt: Build: “What I need is to rest.”
exercises.no: “Lo que necesito es descansar” — the cleft frames the whole idea.

exercises.prompt_en: It was they who decided it.
exercises.hint: Relative for plural people, agreeing with ellos.
exercises.no: For plural people the relative agrees: “Fueron ellos quienes…”.

exercises.prompt: Match each focus type to its relative word.
